proof_readings.assessment: Every restriction to the root orbit belongs to the supported symmetric subgroup; cancellation realizes every complementary induced permutation inside H. Disjoint supports yield an internal direct product.
For b in both root orbits, the supported transposition(a b) lies in both selected groups; input IP places it in the common-label group. The b=a case uses identity.

After cancelling the restriction on the common root orbit, a remaining permutation cannot cross sides: any crossing would start in both root supports and hence in the pointwise fixed intersection. Its two restrictions belong to the corresponding input groups, whose full IP applies. Empty supports, singleton root orbits and distinct marks are covered.
An old point either joins the enlarged root orbit or remains in its original complementary orbit. In each case the requisite supported symmetric group remains available for every subset of labels.

Distinct ports and acyclic incidence ensure each leaf attachment has exactly one point in common with the existing set. Induction uses the preserved point condition. N=sum n_v-|E|, r=sum r_v, and |E|=|V|-1 prove the displayed formula. No exhaustive fixed-deficit classification follows.

Conjugating the pure transposition by the subgroup fixing the root supplies every star transposition on its orbit. For concatenated string markings, only the consecutive endpoint marks can have overlapping support across the joint.

The pure bridge plus disjoint side actions supplies all bipartite transpositions, hence the full symmetric factor. Read literal source pp1,2,4,5,6; independently viewed pp1,2 diagrams, confirming label0 occurs only in the pure leaf. Thm1.1 and Lemmas3.1,3.2 follow with the stated literal hypotheses.

The impure-leaf example is expressly borrowed from source p6. Two-point overlap and cyclic assembly examples demonstrate why hypotheses cannot simply be deleted. Entire Section4 remains unpaid; no whole L010 recovery, compression factor, priority or conjecture resolution is claimed.
